text: Mama came home from the hospital with a tiny bundle in a yellow blanket. Baby Theo had a squished pink face and the smallest fingers Maya had ever seen. Pip peeked over the edge and hiccuped one quiet golden sparkle. "He's so little," Pip whispered.

Baby Theo cried and cried, and everyone rushed to him. Maya's chest felt tight and grumbly. "Sometimes I want Mama all to myself," she told Pip. Pip nodded. "Let's tell her. Big feelings get smaller when you share them with a grown-up."

The big moving truck rumbled away with the Pillow Fort folded inside a box marked MAYA'S THINGS. The old house looked empty and echoey. Maya pressed her hand on her bedroom wall. "Goodbye, room," she whispered. "Thank you for all the sleeps."

On the first night in the new house, thunder grumbled outside the window. The new room made new creaky sounds, and Pip hiccuped a whole shower of golden sparkles. Maya hugged him close. "Let's count slow breaths until the rumbles roll away," she said.

Papa's airplane had flown him far away for a work trip. Tonight his face popped up on the tablet, and he waved from his hotel room. "I can see the same moon from here," Papa said. Maya pressed her nose to the window and waved at the moon too.

Grandma's visit meant a crackly fire in the fireplace, with the safety screen tucked in front. Mama added one more log while everyone stayed back on the rug. Grandma told stories about when Mama was little and lost her shoe in a puddle. Maya laughed until her toes curled.

Maya's best friend Leo had moved far away to a city by the ocean. The swings at the park felt too quiet without him. "Missing someone means you love them," Pip said softly. Together they drew Leo a picture of Moonberry Hill to mail tomorrow.

Mommy and Daddy lived in two different houses now, but they both tucked Maya in with the very same song. At Daddy's house, the squeaky stairs said hello. "Two homes means two Pillow Forts," Pip said, hiccuping a happy sparkle.

Big brother Sam had a fever and a scratchy throat, so he rested in bed with a cool cloth on his forehead. Mama gave him his medicine from the little measuring cup. Maya couldn't hug him tonight, so she blew him a kiss from the doorway.

Sam came home from the hospital with a bright dinosaur bandage on his arm. "The nurse was really gentle," he said, "and I was only a little bit scared." Maya tucked her softest blanket around him. Pip hiccuped sparkles all over the dinosaur.

Biscuit the dog had a grey muzzle now, and his legs were slow on the stairs. The vet said he just needed extra rest and gentle pats. So Maya curled up beside him on his cushion. Biscuit snored softly, and Maya's eyelids grew heavy too.
Maya's baby sister came home from the hospital yesterday, and now Maya keeps asking when the baby is going back. Can you tell her a story about being a big sister?
Maya's dad and I are separating, so she'll be spending weekends at his new apartment. Can you make a gentle story about having two homes where everybody still loves her?
Our dog Biscuit is fourteen and the vet says he's getting old and tired. Maya asked me tonight if he's going to die soon. Can we have a calm story about loving an old dog?
